title: Threshold Detector
statement: Build an 8-bit threshold detector that asserts output when the input exceeds a fixed constant value of 100 decimal. The output must be high for 101 and greater, and low for 100 and below. This is a common operation in analog-to-digital and control circuits.
behavior: The logic must be purely combinational.
Purely combinational: outputs must settle after input changes.
Do not depend on initial register values, clocks, or delays.
All outputs must be driven to known 0/1 values for every input case.
constraints: Do not use a sequential comparator or state machine.
hint: Hardcode the threshold comparison with bitwise logic if needed.
